title: Summoned My Labour to Renew
description: Summoned My Labour to Renew in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 321. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sum-moned my la-bour to re-new, And glad to act my part, Lord, in thy name my work I do, And with a sin-gle heart.

lines: And glad to act my part,
Lord, in thy name my work I do,
End of my every action thou,
In all things thee I see:
Whate'er the Father views as thine,
Thy work he then shall own;
Well pleased with me, when mine thou art,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
